questions.question_text: A particle moves along a horizontal axis with a velocity of $v = -14\text{ m/s}$. What is the speed of the particle, and in which direction is it travelling?

options.text: Speed is $14\text{ m/s}$ travelling in the negative direction.
Speed is $14\text{ m/s}$ travelling in the positive direction.
options.why: Takes the magnitude correctly but then discards the minus sign altogether, reading $v = -14$ as motion in the positive direction.

options.text: Speed is $-14\text{ m/s}$ travelling in the negative direction.
options.why: Copies the velocity straight across as the speed, forgetting that speed is the magnitude $|v|$ and can never be negative.

options.text: Speed is $-14\text{ m/s}$ travelling in the positive direction.
options.why: Makes both slips at once: keeps the minus sign on the speed and still assumes the motion must be in the positive direction.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Speed is the magnitude of velocity: } |v| = |-14| = 14\text{ m/s}.$
$\text{The negative sign indicates movement in the negative direction.}$

questions.question_text: A student walks $120\text{ m}$ due north from a flagpole, stops, and then walks $45\text{ m}$ due south. Taking north as the positive direction, what are the student's final displacement from the flagpole and total distance walked?

options.text: Displacement: $+75\text{ m}$; Distance: $165\text{ m}$
Displacement: $+165\text{ m}$; Distance: $75\text{ m}$
options.why: Swaps the definitions of displacement and distance.

options.text: Displacement: $+75\text{ m}$; Distance: $75\text{ m}$
options.why: Equates total distance travelled to the magnitude of net displacement.

options.text: Displacement: $-75\text{ m}$; Distance: $165\text{ m}$
options.why: Assigns the wrong sign to the net displacement north of the origin.

questions.question_text: A particle's motion along a straight line satisfies $x = -9\text{ m}$ and $v = -4\text{ m/s}$. Which statement accurately describes its motion?

options.text: The particle is $9\text{ m}$ to the left of the origin and moving further away from the origin.
The particle is $9\text{ m}$ to the left of the origin and moving towards the origin.
options.why: A negative velocity moves the particle further in the negative direction, not towards the origin.

options.text: The particle is $9\text{ m}$ to the right of the origin and moving towards the origin.
options.why: Misinterprets $x = -9$ as being to the right of the origin.

options.text: The particle is at rest $9\text{ m}$ to the left of the origin.
options.why: Ignores the non-zero velocity $v = -4\text{ m/s}$.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Since } x = -9 < 0\text{, the particle is } 9\text{ m to the left of the origin}.$
$\text{Since } v = -4 < 0\text{, it is moving further left, away from the origin}.$

questions.question_text: A particle moves along a straight line from position $x = 6\text{ m}$ at $t = 0$ to $x = 18\text{ m}$ at $t = 3\text{ s}$, then reverses direction and reaches $x = 10\text{ m}$ at $t = 5\text{ s}$. What is the total distance travelled between $t = 0$ and $t = 5\text{ s}$?

options.text: $20\text{ m}$
$4\text{ m}$
options.why: Calculates net displacement $x(5) - x(0) = 10 - 6 = 4$ instead of total distance.

options.text: $12\text{ m}$
options.why: Only computes the distance of the first leg before reversal.

options.text: $28\text{ m}$
options.why: Incorrectly sums coordinates $18 + 10 = 28$ without subtracting starting position.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Leg 1 distance} = |18 - 6| = 12\text{ m}$
$\text{Leg 2 distance} = |10 - 18| = 8\text{ m}$
$\text{Total distance} = 12 + 8 = 20\text{ m}$

questions.question_text: Two objects $X$ and $Y$ have velocities $v_X = +25\text{ m/s}$ and $v_Y = -30\text{ m/s}$ respectively. Which comparison of their velocities and speeds is correct?

options.text: $X$ has a greater velocity than $Y$, but $Y$ has a greater speed than $X$.
$Y$ has both a greater velocity and a greater speed than $X$.
options.why: Treats $-30$ as numerically greater than $+25$ in signed velocity.

options.text: $X$ has both a greater velocity and a greater speed than $Y$.
options.why: Ignores the magnitude of $v_Y$, which gives $Y$ a speed of $30\text{ m/s} > 25\text{ m/s}$.

options.text: $X$ and $Y$ have equal speeds because direction does not affect motion.
options.why: The speeds are $25\text{ m/s}$ and $30\text{ m/s}$, which are not equal.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Velocities: } +25 > -30\text{, so } X\text{ has greater velocity.}$
$\text{Speeds: } |v_Y| = 30 > |v_X| = 25\text{, so } Y\text{ has greater speed.}$

questions.question_text: At what point is a particle moving along the $x$-axis classified as "instantaneously at rest"?

options.text: When its velocity $v = 0$.
When its displacement $x = 0$.
options.why: Displacement $x = 0$ means the particle is at the origin, not at rest.

options.text: When time $t = 0$.
options.why: Time $t = 0$ represents the initial instant, not necessarily zero velocity.

options.text: When its acceleration $a = 0$.
options.why: Acceleration $a = 0$ means constant velocity, not necessarily zero velocity.

questions.solution_text: $\text{A particle is at rest or stationary at the instant its velocity is zero } (v = 0).$

questions.question_text: A particle moves from $x = -3\text{ m}$ to $x = 5\text{ m}$ in a straight line without reversing direction. What are its net displacement and distance travelled?

options.text: Displacement is $+8\text{ m}$ and distance is $8\text{ m}$.
Displacement is $+2\text{ m}$ and distance is $8\text{ m}$.
options.why: Calculates $-3 + 5 = 2$ instead of $x_2 - x_1 = 5 - (-3) = 8$.

options.text: Displacement is $+8\text{ m}$ and distance is $2\text{ m}$.
options.why: Incorrectly calculates distance as $|5 + (-3)| = 2$.

options.text: Displacement is $-8\text{ m}$ and distance is $8\text{ m}$.
options.why: Reverses the direction of displacement from initial to final position.

questions.question_text: A particle moves along a line such that $x(0) = -2\text{ m}$, $x(4) = 14\text{ m}$, and $x(6) = 6\text{ m}$, with a single turnaround at $t = 4\text{ s}$. What is the ratio of total distance travelled to the magnitude of net displacement over $[0, 6\text{ s}]$?

options.why: Assumes distance equals magnitude of displacement without accounting for reversal.
Computes distance as $16\text{ m}$ instead of summing both legs $16 + 8 = 24\text{ m}$.
Arithmetic error in evaluating distance or displacement magnitude.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Leg 1 distance} = |14 - (-2)| = 16\text{ m}$
$\text{Leg 2 distance} = |6 - 14| = 8\text{ m}$
$\text{Total distance} = 16 + 8 = 24\text{ m}$
$\text{Net displacement} = 6 - (-2) = +8\text{ m}$
$\text{Ratio} = \dfrac{24}{8} = 3:1$
